name: Box Personal Pro
tagline: Store and share files from a user-owned server with expiring links

tiers.name: Individual
tiers.limits: 10 GB storage; 250 MB maximum upload; 1 file version; 5 Box Sign requests/month.

tiers.name: Personal Pro
tiers.limits: 100 GB storage; 5 GB maximum upload; 10 file versions; 15 Box Sign requests/month.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 10 GB storage, 250 MB maximum upload, 1 file version and 5 Box Sign requests/month
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual price is the effective monthly rate
pricing.hiddenCosts: Shared-link download bandwidth is capped at 10 GB/user/month on Individual and 2 TB/user/month on Personal Pro; aggregate ingress plus egress is also limited to 1 TB and 2 TB per user/month respectively.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Box Personal Pro, store and share files from a user-owned server with expiring links. The hard boundary is enterprise-grade sharing, previews, integrations, security, and compliance, plus reliability, durability, and cross-device sync.
coreLoopDIY: Store and share files from a user-owned server with expiring links, back up selected folders, encrypt files client-side, track versions, and restore from user-owned object storage.
whatYouLose: enterprise-grade sharing, previews, integrations, security, and compliance
ongoingBurden: chunking, encryption, conflict detection, versions, garbage collection, bandwidth, restore drills, monitoring, billing, and disaster recovery
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Box Personal Pro because storage subscriptions sell confidence that files will still exist after a lost device, bad sync, or provider incident. The recurring cost buys chunking, encryption, conflict detection, versions, garbage collection, bandwidth, restore drills, monitoring, billing, and disaster recovery, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Nextcloud
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source file sync and collaboration server.

alternatives.name: Nextcloud Files
alternatives.desc: Files, expiring links, desktop sync, mobile apps, and a server you now have to babysit.

facts.install: Deploy Nextcloud All-in-One with Docker, or perform a manual web-server, PHP and database installation
facts.dataFormat: Files live in the configured local data directory or object storage; metadata, shares, versions and application state live in a supported SQL database
facts.gapVsPaid: External collaboration and administration are less polished than Box, and the user becomes responsible for uptime, upgrades and backups.
facts.setupBlocker: A server plus Docker or a full web stack, DNS and TLS, and a plan for upgrades, backups and storage failures

alternatives.name: OpenCloud
alternatives.desc: A leaner self-hosted file cloud with expiring public links and fewer moving database parts.

facts.install: Use the documented Docker Compose and Traefik stack; a single-binary deployment is also possible
facts.dataFormat: The base deployment stores file data and metadata in its configured POSIX instance directory; an optional decomposed backend stores blobs in S3 and metadata on POSIX storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its integration ecosystem and administration are younger and thinner than Box's, while all server operations become the user's job.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker, a domain and open ports, reverse-proxy and TLS configuration, and operational responsibility for the storage directory

alternatives.name: Seafile Community Edition
alternatives.desc: Fast sync, version history, and password-expiring links; the server is still your weekend.

facts.install: Deploy the Community Edition with the official Docker Compose stack
facts.dataFormat: File libraries are stored as deduplicated blocks with Git-like repository, commit and filesystem objects rather than ordinary folders, while metadata lives in relational databases
facts.gapVsPaid: Its web collaboration and integration layer is less rich than Box's, and server-side files live in Seafile's internal block format.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose, MariaDB, Caddy or another proxy, a domain and TLS, plus coordinated backups of both databases and block storage

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Personal Pro plan and a single-user encrypted backup DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Box Personal Pro in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, MinIO, and a Tauri 2 sync client; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: store and share files from a user-owned server with expiring links, back up selected folders, encrypt files client-side, track versions, and restore from user-owned object storage.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Build a desktop client that watches explicitly selected folders and ignores configured patterns.
Chunk, hash, compress, and encrypt files locally before uploading to the configured object store.
Store version metadata, tombstones, device identifiers, and integrity checks in PostgreSQL.
Provide upload and restore queues with pause, retry, bandwidth limits, and resumable transfers.
Add file history, point-in-time restore, key export, storage usage, and scheduled restore tests.
Document the failure model and make clear that one server is not a complete backup strategy.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out multi-provider consumer sync at global scale.
Deliberately leave out guaranteed durability or ransomware recovery.
Deliberately leave out shared-drive administration, mobile apps, and enterprise compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
